narrative: A macro-laden Invoice_April.docm opened by m.reyes on FIN-WS-07 spawned an encoded PowerShell stager (sysmon.jsonl:1-2). The stager inhibited recovery by deleting volume shadow copies and backup catalogs via vssadmin/wbadmin/bcdedit (sysmon.jsonl:4-6), then ran svch0st.exe to encrypt 8 finance documents to a .locky extension (sysmon.jsonl:7-14) and dropped READ_ME_TO_DECRYPT.txt (sysmon.jsonl:15). Throughout, FIN-WS-07 beaconed to a known Locky C2 at 203.0.113.77 (fw_traffic.jsonl:1-4), and the file server lost the encrypted shares and its nightly snapshot (app_payments.jsonl:1-2). Blast radius: FIN-WS-07, the m.reyes identity, and the finance documents.
decoy: An EICAR antivirus test file (eicar.com) was downloaded on IT-LAB-02 (sysmon.jsonl:3) and lit up AV dashboards. It looks like patient zero but is the standard benign EICAR test artifact (rated benign in threat_intel.csv:2), and IT-LAB-02 shows zero shadow-copy deletion or .locky encryption. A correct agent must NOT attribute the ransomware to the EICAR host and must self-correct to FIN-WS-07.
root_cause: A malicious Office macro spawned a PowerShell stager that deleted shadow copies and encrypted finance documents on FIN-WS-07, beaconing to a Locky C2.
